Commentary.Commentary: Rangana Herath was the pick of the bowlers as he kept the batsmen guessing with his natural variations. Kumara bended his back and was impressive as well. It is a good track to bat on and the Sri Lankans will be confident of putting an impressive show. Can Zimbabwe take some early wickets to put pressure on the hosts? Join us shortly to find out.

It was majorly due to the brilliant batting strokeplay of Craig Ervine that they managed to get past the 350-run mark. He batted sensibly and shepherded the lower middle order smartly. The hosts after getting off to a good start on Day 1 lost the plot somewhat but will be happy that they didn't allow the tourists to get to 400.

Just what the doctor ordered for Sri Lanka this morning. They wrapped up the visitors in a jiffy, only allowing them to add 12 to their overnight total. Herath with his 30th fifer broke the stubborn 74-run stand between Craig Ervine and Donald Tiripano. Eventually it was Lahiru Kumara who took the wicket of the southpaw to end the innings.

OUT! That is it! Sri Lanka have wrapped things up quickly today. Kumara gets his second. Ervine walks back to the hut after an absolutely brilliant innings. Lahiru bangs it in short outside off, Craig tries to ramp it over third man but it goes to Dilruwan Parera who runs to his right and takes a well-judged catch. Kumara is pumped. ZIMBABWE HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 356.
Good length outside off, the batsman guides it down to third man but does not run.
Back of a length outside off, Craig taps it to point and opts not to run.
A tad fuller on off, Ervine defends it off the front foot.
Loopy ball on off, Mpofu defends it off the front foot.
Chris Mpofu is the last man in. Dickwella and Mendis are having a conversation. Might be trying to get under the nerves of the tailender. A silly point comes in place as well.

OUT! 5-fer for Herath! Sri Lanka get the early breakthrough they wanted. Full ball outside off, Tiripano tries to play the reverse sweep but it comes off his glove and goes straight to Karunaratne at first slip who takes a safe catch. The partnership has been broken and who else but the wily veteran has done it. This is his 30th five wicket-haul in Test cricket. Tiripano walks back dejected. What was his pet shot throughout this innings eventually brought his downfall.

Almost a chop on! Loopy ball on off, Tiripano tries to defend it off the front foot but gets an inside edge. The ball was going to hit the stumps but Tiripano does well to kick the ball out of the way.
Drags his length back a little, turns away from the batsman. Tiripano punches it off the back foot through covers for a couple.
And again! Floated on middle, Ervine reverse sweeps it but not off the middle through point for a run.
He has played that reverse sweep to great effect. Tosses it on off, Ervine reverse sweeps it through backward point for a couple. That was good running by the batsmen.
Stays around the wicket to the right-hander and bowls a full ball down the leg side. Tiripano does not bother playing a shot at it.
Back of a length outside off, Craig guides it towards point for a run.
A tad fuller on off, Ervine defends it back to the bowler.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Full and down the leg side, Ervine misses his flick and the ball goes through to the keeper.

BIG APPEAL! Lands it on a length, coming into the batsman. Ervine tries to play it on the leg side but misses and is struck on the pads. The Lankans appeal but the umpire gives it not out. Might be missing leg.
Quicker on the stumps, Tiripano drives it to long on for a run.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floats it up outside off, Tiripano nudges it towards point for a run.
Tossed up delivery, Ervine reverse sweeps it through point for a single.
Sweeps it with the spin through backward square leg for a couple.
Tosses it on middle, Ervine tries to flick it but misses and is struck on the pads.
Rangana Herath to bowl from the other end.
The move of getting a leg gully in almost pays off. A tad fuller on leg stump, Tiripano flicks it on the bounce to Chandimal at leg gully.
Bangs it in short on middle, Tiripano ducks under it.
A tad fuller outside off, Tiripano covers the line of the ball and defends it off the front foot.
Good length on off, the batsman defends it solidly.
Just behind a length angling into the batsman, Craig flicks it through square leg for a run.
Right on the money first up. Fullish on middle, Ervine looks to defend it but gets it off the inner half to mid-wicket.

We are set to get underway. The players and the umpires come out in the middle. The Sri Lankan team is in a huddle. Craig Ervine and Donald Tiripano to continue their innings. Can the southpaw score his maiden Test double ton? Lahiru Kumara to bowl first up this morning. One slip and a gully in place. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Alistair Campbell and Russel Arnold feel this is a really good surface. Mention there are a little footmarks but not threatening enough. Inform there are no rough patches on the good length area. Opine it is going to remain a good batting surface today.

Sri Lanka on the other hand will be aiming to bowl the tourists out as soon as possible. They will bank on Rangana Herath to clean the tail up in a jiffy. It is a good track to bat on but will keep slowing down as the game progresses. Both sides are on equal terms at the moment but the one which dominates the morning session will most likely hold the aces. Expect a thrilling day of cricketing action!

Hello and a warm welcome for Day 2 of the one-off Test between Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe. Though the visitors lost 8 wickets yesterday, they ensured they do not miss out on scoring opportunities. Craig Ervine is standing in the middle like a rock and has got good support from Donald Tiripano who has frustrated the bowlers. The southpaw will look to score freely and take the total close to 400.
...Day 2, Session 1...

Earlier in the day, Sri Lanka reduced Zimbabwe to 70/4 and were cruising at that moment. However, the home side failed to capitalize after that. Craig Ervine and the lower middle order played the sweeps and the reverse sweeps to great effect and scored at a brisk rate. The away side will be the happier of the two at the moment and have momentum on their side. The hosts would want to come out tomorrow and bowl the visitors out as soon as possible. Join us for day 2 tomorrow at 1000 local (0430 GMT). Till then, cheers!

Sri Lanka on the other hand will be disappointed with the fact that they have let the visitors off the hook. They were not quite disciplined with the ball in the last session and gave away too many runs for their liking. Rangana Herath was the pick of the bowlers today as he picked up a 4-fer.

Craig Ervine walks off to a standing ovation by his teammates and what an innings it has been from him. He has recorded his career-best score and also helped Zimbabwe to finish the day on a high. They scored quickly in this session and lost only two wickets. Ervine was well supported by Malcolm Waller and Donald Tiripano towards the end of the day. Graeme Cremer had mentioned after the toss that he would like something above 350 and they are certainly close to that.
FOUR! Half-tracker and duly punished! Tiripano uses the depth of the crease, lines this one up and hammers it over mid-wicket for a boundary. Ends the day on a high. THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 1!
Slower through the air, Donald drives it to mid on where the fielder moves to his left and does well to stop it with a dive.
Loopy ball on off, Tiripano puts his head down and defends it calmly.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Floated outside off, eased towards point for a single.
Tossed up around off, Ervine lunges forward in defense.
Straying on the pads, Ervine turns it around the corner. Lakmal there fumbles to concede the single. First 150+ score for Ervine in Tests. He has been solid as a rock. A muted celebration from him.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fullish delivery on middle and leg, Ervine comes down the track and jams it out.
Quicker one coming into Tiripano. He camps back and dabs it past first slip. A single taken.
A bit short around off, Tiripano punches it towards the fielder at short extra cover who misfields and parries it to mid off. However, no single conceded.
Floated on middle, worked to front of square on the leg side for a single.
A touch short around off, Donald rocks back and punches it to short extra cover.
A silly point in place for the batsman.
Tossed up outside off, turned through mid-wicket for a single.
Loopy ball on middle, blocked to the leg side.
Arm ball on off, Ervine keeps it out.
Flighted delivery on off, Ervine prods forward to defend it.
Prods forward to the tossed up delivery and defends it.
Tossed up around leg stump, Tiripano opts to pad it away. A stifled appeal for an LBW is turned down.
Shortish delivery outside off, Ervine cuts it through point for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Floated on middle, Donald reverse sweeps it to third man for a run. He continues to frustrate the Lankans.
Tossed up around the pads, worked towards square leg for a run.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.

A loud shout for an LBW turned down! Quicker one, coming in with the arm. Tiripano hangs back to defend but is struck on the pads. The umpire turns down the loud shout. The replays show that it was going down leg. Wise decision not to waste another review.
Coming in with the arm, Tiripano defends it off the inner half towards short leg. Mendis kneels and looks to take it but it falls just short of him.
Floated in line of the stumps, Ervine goes for the reverse sweep but doesn't get on top of the bounce. Gets it uppishly to third man for a run.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Flatter delivery outside off, going away with the angle. Ervine goes for the cut but gets it off the bottom half towards first slip.
Tossed up around the pads, worked to the leg side.
A bit shorter this time, cut through point for a run.
A bit flatter this time in line of the stumps, whipped through front of square on the leg side for a couple.
Tossed up around off, reverse swept to backward point.
Ervine stays back and defends this one.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads

Not out! Infact it has come straight off the glove! Sri Lanka lose a review! Tosses this one around off and it comes in with the arm. Ervine kneels and looks to reverse sweep but seems to have missed it. Umpire Ian Gould shakes his head instantly. However, Chandimal opts for the review after having a chat with the bowler. The replays show that it has struck the gloves. That ends the story there itself.
A review for LBW has been taken against Ervine. It might not have hit him in line.
Dilruwan Perera is back into the attack.
A bit short around off, defended off the back foot to the off side.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished! Half-tracker on middle and leg, Tiripano hammers it through square leg for a rocketing boundary. This is the highest 9th wicket partnership for Zimbabwe against Sri Lanka in Tests. Good stuff!
Flatter delivery on off, Ervine kneels and adjusts well to paddle it to fine leg. A run taken.
Drifting down the leg side, helped on its way to short fine leg for a run.
Tossed up on middle, Tiripano hangs back and defends it stoutly.
Lakmal comes around the wicket and gets this one to shape in sharply. Ervine works it behind square on the leg side for a run.

FOUR! Beautiful! Back of a length delivery angling away from the southpaw. He stands tall and punches it with authority through covers and the ball whistles away to the fence. He is pleasing to watch when he plays those. Great timing!
Good length delivery on off, Ervine hangs back and keeps it out.
Slanting across Ervine once again and he doesn't fiddle with it. He has mixed caution with aggression to great effect today.
Length delivery angling across Craig. He covers his off pole to allow it through.
Back of a length delivery around off, Ervine punches it to short extra cover.
FOUR! Handy runs these! The tailender certainly can bat. Tossed up in line of the stumps, Tiripano executes the reverse sweep really well and plays it past short third man to pick up a boundary.
This one pitches outside off and skids on. Tiripano lets it go.
Coming in with the arm, Tiripano prods forward to defend but gets an inside edge to short leg.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Floated outside off, Ervine reverse sweeps it to third man for a brace.
Tossed up delivery outside off, Ervine hangs back and defends it to the leg side.
Rangana Herath is brought back into the attack.
Fullish delivery on off, driven crisply to mid on.
Good length delivery around off, Donald hangs back and defends it.
Fuller in length and shaping away from Tiripano. Played with an open face to cover-point.
Fullish and curving in nicely into Ervine. He uses the depth of the crease to turn it behind square on the leg side. A run taken.
FOUR! Shot! Half-volley outside off, Ervine leans ahead and strokes it through covers for an exquisite boundary. He has been sensational with his strokeplay today.
Fullish delivery attacking the stumps, Ervine keeps it out.
Suranga Lakmal is back on the field and he will bowl with the second new ball.
Second new ball is available and it has been taken straightaway.

Tiripano leans forward to defend this one but misses. The ball brushes the pad and lobs to the left side of Mendis and falls on the ground. The bat probably came in contact with the pad and hence the sound.
Fullish on middle, played with soft hands down the track.
Floated around off, Tiripano prods forward to defend but gets it off the inner half to short leg.
No ball! The overstepping issue is haunting him. He keeps on repeating the same mistake. Low full toss on off, stroked to long on for a single.
A bit short outside off, cut towards point.
Identical to the last delivery and Ervine doesn't bother playing a shot to it.
Flatter delivery outside off, turning away. Ervine plants his front foot across and sees it through.
Lakmal has been seen walking off the field. His knee might be making him feel a little uncomfortable.
Fullish outside off, Tiripano lunges forward in defense.
Loopy delivery outside off, Donald stays back and defends it solidly.
Floated on middle, Tiripano defends it with his bat and pad close together.
Tossed up outside off, patted to short extra cover.
Floated in line of the stumps, defended solidly off the front foot.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flatter delivery outside off, Ervine doesn't fiddle with it.
Outside off, left alone.
Slower through the air outside off, Ervine pushes at it tentatively but gets an outside edge towards short third man.
Floated in line of the stumps, Ervine lunges forward in defense.
Fullish on middle and leg, Tiripano turns it through mid-wicket for a single.
Fullish on off, Ervine paddles it deftly to fine leg for a single.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Fullish outside off, Tiripano goes for the reverse sweep but gets it off the bottom half and back to the pads.
A touch short on off, Ervine punches it uppishly past the right side of the bowler. A run taken. 300 up for Zimbabwe.
FOUR! Ervine has used the reverse swept to good effect today! Floated on middle, Ervine reverse sweeps it with authority and the ball races to the third man fence.
Straying on the pads, nudged behind square on the leg side for a single.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Floated outside off, Tiripano stretches forward and blocks it.
No ball! A bit short on middle, Ervine camps back and punches it to long off for a run. Oh my word! Gunaratne has overstepped once again.
Fullish on middle an leg, Donald clips it through mid-wicket for a run.
Loopy ball around leg stump, spinning down. Tiripano looks to glance it but misses.
The batsman has driven it through mid off.
Floated on middle, played with soft hands to the bowler.
Fullish on off, paddle swept to fine leg for a run.
Well bowled! Floated outside off, Donald plays for the turn but it goes straight on to beat his outside edge.
FOUR! Nice improvisation! Tossed up on off, Tiripano kneels and reverse sweeps it through short third man for a boundary.
Slow through the air around off, Tiripano camps back and cuts it through point for a couple.
Fullish on middle and leg, flicked to short leg.
A bit short outside off, punched through point for a run.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Fullish on middle and leg, defended solidly.
Donald Tiripano is the next man in.

OUT! Gunaratne picks up his second wicket! He has a habit of breaking partnerships and he does it again. Tossed this one nicely around off and gets it to turn in. Cremer goes for the drive but misses. The ball goes through the gap between bat and pad and hits the off stump. The umpires check for the front foot but it is fine. They also check whether the bails came off or whether Dickwella's gloves were involved. It shows that the bail came off on impact with the ball. Sri Lanka will be aiming to bowl the visitors out under 300.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tossed up on middle and leg, Cremer turns it to Mendis at short leg. He picks it up and aims at the bowler's end but misses. The mid off fielder backs up well. He almost hit Gunaratne with his throw.
Almost dragged it back! Length delivery outside off, Ervine pushes at it but is early into his stroke. Gets a thick inside edge past the leg stump. A run taken.
Tossed up on middle and leg, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
No ball! Fullish ball on middle, Cremer eases it to mid off. Gunaratne has once again overstepped.
Lakmal seems to have some issue with his left knee. He must have hurt it while diving in the last ball of the previous over. The physio is out and he will need some treatment.
Loopy delivery outside off, Cremer taps it to covers. Lakmal dives to his right and stops it. A single taken.
A bit short around off, Ervine cuts it to sweeper cover for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floated around off, played with soft hands to the right of Perera.
Tossed up outside off, dealt with easily by Ervine.
Loopy delivery outside off, Ervine lunges forward in defense.

Time for Drinks. A fast-paced hour of play with Ervine going past his second Test ton. Good passage of play for Zimbabwe as they have scored runs briskly. Sri Lanka will be aiming to take the remaining three wickets quickly and keep the visitors under the 325-run mark.
Full on middle and leg, eased towards mid on.
Short delivery, pulled behind square on the leg side for a couple.
Slow through the air on middle and leg, turned towards Mendis at short leg who dives to his right to make a terrific stop. He is sharp as a hawk in that region.
No ball! Fullish on off, Ervine kneels and paddles it around the corner for a run. It is called a no ball as Gunaratne overstepped.
Beaten! Floated delivery around off, Craig prods forward to defend but is foxed by the sharp away turn. A good take by Dickwella behind the stumps.
Similar length delivery outside off, Ervine leans forward and pats it to the off side.
Full length delivery in line of the stumps, Ervine keeps it out.
Asela Gunaratne is back into the attack.
Floated outside off, Graeme lunges forward in defense.

That could have been a wicket! Drifting into Cremer. He nudges it towards Mendis at short leg. He crouches low to take it but the ball hits his boot. It then goes onto brush his shin pad and lobs behind. Kusal shows good reflexes and dives to take it but is not able to do so.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Perera sees Ervine coming and darts it around his pads. He looks to play it across but gets it off the inner half to short fine leg. A sharp single taken.
Tossed up outside off, Ervine puts his head down and defends it calmly.
Fullish delivery on off, paddle swept to short fine leg.
Quicker one on middle and leg, defended off the inner half to short leg.
Slow through the air outside off, Ervine brings out the reverse sweep and executes it well. Gets it to deep backward point for a run.
Quicker one around off, Craig covers the line to defend it.
Floated outside off, Craig shuffles a touch and blocks it solidly.
Ervine uses his feet to the tossed up delivery outside off and eases it towards mid on.
Slow through the air on middle, defended to short leg.
A slight delay. A kite had fallen into the field. Angelo Mathews hands it back to the ball boy.
Shortish delivery outside off, Ervine rocks back and cuts it to sweeper cover for a run.
A bit wider outside off and it is dealt with ease again.
Flighted delivery outside off, tapped to short extra cover.
Drifting into Craig. He turns it to the left of the bowler.
Fullish outside off, played with soft hands to covers.
A bit short on off, pushed off the back foot to the off side.
Flatter on off, defended off the back foot.
Tossed up on off, patted to covers.
Quicker one drifting on with the arm, played from the inner half past short leg.
Landed on middle and leg, kept out.

FOUR! Close shave! Flatter delivery on off, turning away. Cremer flashes and flashes hard at it. Gets it just past the diving Karunaratne to his right and through to the fence. If he had taken that, it would have been an outstanding catch.
Tossed up in line of the stumps, Cremer lunges forward in defense.
Flighted outside off, pushed to the right of the bowler who does well to stop with a dive.
Well bowled! Floated on off, turning away. Ervine prods forward to defend but gets an outside edge that carries on the bounce to first slip. He played that with soft hands and that saved him.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tossed up outside off, spinning away. Ervine comes forward and lets it go.
Drifting down the leg side, Cremer turns it through square leg for a run.
Tossed up on middle, defended solidly off the front foot.
Bowled on the pads, Cremer flicks it through short fine leg for a run.
Bowled outside off, Cremer lets it through to the keeper.
Angles it into the pads, Cremer flicks it through mid wicket for no runs.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tosses it up on off, Ervine drives it through mid on for a run.
Very full on leg stump, the batsman drives it to wide mid on for a run.
A tad short on middle, Cremer punches it to long on for a run.
Bowled on off, Cremer defends it by covering the line of the ball.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Dances down the wicket and drives it back to the bowler. The bowler collects the ball and throws it at the striker's end.
Floats it on off, the batsman defends it solidly.
Tosses it up on off, Cremer defends it off the front foot.
Quicker on off, Ervine drives it back to the bowler.
Flighted ball on middle, Craig defends it solidly.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Floats it on a length on middle, Cremer gets it off the inner half through square leg for a run.
The skipper, Graeme Cremer comes out to bat.

OUT! JAFFA! This is an absolute beauty by the veteran. He has got a 4-fer. Tosses it on middle, Waller plays for the ball which goes straight with the arm but the ball turns away and hits the off stump. Waller has to depart after playing a good knock. A 65-run stand has been broken by Herath.
Floats it on leg stump, Waller works it on the leg side.
Quciker on off, comes in with the angle. Ervine tries to defend it but gets an inside edge and the ball rolls to fine leg.
Bowls it on the stumps, Malcolm sweeps it through square leg for a run.
Flatter on off, Waller pushes it through covers for a couple.
Tosses it up on off, goes on with the arm. Waller prods forward and tries to defend it but gets beaten.
Short and outside off, Waller tries to cut but gets beaten.
A low full toss on leg stump, Ervine flicks it through backward square leg for a run.
Dilruwan Perera comes back into the attack.
Flighted ball outside off, Waller guides it towards point.
Slower through the air, the batsman defends it off the front foot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Very full ball on off, Malcolm drives it to mid off.
Loopy ball on middle, Waller defends it off the inner half to square leg.
Angles it down the leg side, Waller flicks it through short fine leg for a couple.
Back of a length outside off, Waller guides it to backward point for a run.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Bowled on the pads, Ervine flicks it through mid-wicket. Mathews gives it chase and this time he manages to pull the ball back in. Three runs taken by the batsmen.
FOUR! Short ball on leg stump, Ervine goes for the pull but gets a top edge over the keeper for a boundary. Kumara is getting frustrated, he has no luck on his side.

Bowls a length ball on leg stump, Ervine misses the flick and is struck on the pads. The Lankans appeal but the umpire turns it down. After a long chat between the teammates they opt not to review. Replays show it was pitched outside leg.
Bangs it in short outside off, Ervine lets it through to the keeper.
Floats it on off, Waller defends it solidly.
2nd Test hundred for Craig Ervine.
Full on the pads, Ervine sweeps it through short fine leg for a run. He brings up a well-deserved 100. It has been a vital knock by him and he needs to carry on.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
50-run stand between Craig Ervine and Malcolm Waller.
Loopy ball on off, Waller drives it through covers for a run.
Tosses it up on middle, Waller defends it off the front foot.
FOUR! POOR LENGTH! Short ball around off, Waller camps back and cuts it through point for a boundary.
Sprays down the leg side, Ervine misses his flick.
FOUR! Lahiru is unlucky here. Bowls a yorker outside off, Ervine gets a bottom edge over the keeper for a boundary. He moves onto 99.
Bowls a well-directed bouncer, Ervine does well to evade it.
A tad shorter outside off, Waller guides it through point for a run.
Full ball on off stump, Ervine drives it towards wide mid on for a run.
Good length on off, Ervine defends it off the front foot.
Flatter on off, Waller plays it to point.
Played to the point region by the batsman. One run added to the total.

BIG APPEAL! Bowls it slower on leg stump, turning back in. Ervine goes back and tries to work it on the leg side but is struck on the pads. There is a huge appeal but the umpire gives it not out. After a chat with his teammates, Chandimal decides not to review. It looked a little high.
Tosses it up on  off, Waller tries to drive it but gets it off the inner half towards mid on for a run.
Bowls it on the pads, Waller flicks it to mid-wicket.
Innovation! Plays the reverse sweep through point for a run.
A tad fuller on off, Waller pushes it towards mid off for a run. 9 from the over a good one for Zimbabwe.
Bowled on the pads, Waller works it on the leg side for a run.

FOUR! Good length outside off, Waller drives it through covers. Mathews gives it chase from mid off but only comes second best and the ball rolls over the fence. Mathews should have put in a better effort.
Short and angling into the batsman, Craig pulls it down to fine leg for a run.
A tad fuller on off, Waller drives it through covers for a run.
Shorter in length on middle, Ervine pulls it through mid-wicket for a run.
Lahiru Kumara will bowl from the other end.
FOUR! Gives it air and bowls it full on off, Waller drives it through covers for a boundary.
The batsman has punched that ball through the offside.
Good effort from Lahiru! Plays the reverse sweep through short third man. Kumara runs to his right and does well to keep the ball in play. He saves a run for his team.
Floats it on off, Ervine defends it off the front foot.
Drags his length back a little outside off, the batsman cuts it through covers for a couple.
Starts off with a tossed up delivery on off, Ervine defends it off the front foot.

We are back for the final session. Craig Ervine and Malcolm Waller to continue their innings. 35 overs are left in the day. Rangana Herath to bowl first up after tea. A slip and short leg in place. Here we go...
...Day 1, Session 3...

Whenever the away side has looked like settling into a rhythm, a false shot has pegged them back. They only have to blame themselves for this. Craig Ervine is playing a great hand but he needs support from the other end to take the visitors past 300. Sri Lanka will look to come out after the tea break and clean the lower order in a jiffy. Join us shortly.

A better session for Zimbabwe as they scored at a healthy run rate while losing two wickets. They came out in the afternoon session and played with intent. The duo of Ervine and Raza started scoring freely but the wily old customer, Herath deceived the latter to send him packing. Moor came in and looked decent in the middle but he was guilty of throwing his wicket away.
Bowls it on a length outside off, Ervine guides it towards point for a run. TEA ON DAY 1.

Lands it on a length on middle, Ervine plays it back to the bowler who has a shy at the non-striker's end but misses. Ian Gould the umpire had to jump out of the way as the ball would have hit his shin. He is not happy about the throw.
Good length on off, Craig defends it off the back foot.
The batsman has driven it to mid off.
Length ball angling across the batsman, Ervine pokes at it but gets beaten.

Good length delivery, Waller punches it through covers and attempts for the third run. Lakmal collects the throw and deflects it back onto the stumps at the bowler's end. Appeals but the umpire is not interested. The batsman was running too wide of the wicket and he was struggling while running the third.
FOUR! POOR LENGTH! Short and on the stumps, Ervine flat bats it over mid on for a boundary. He is playing a fine knock. He needs support from the other end.
Short ball on leg stump, Malcolm flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
Drags his length back on middle, turns back in a little. Waller punches it to covers.
Very full on middle, Waller drives it back to the bowler.
FOUR! A low full toss on middle, Waller goes down on one knee and sweeps it through square leg for a boundary.
Tosses it up outside off, Malcolm drives it through cover-point for a couple. 200 up for Zimbabwe.
Bowls it very full on off, Waller drives it through covers for a run.
Lands it on a length outside off, Waller drives it through cover-point for a couple.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
A tad fuller on off, Malcolm drives it crisply to covers.
Full on off this time, Waller pushes it to mid off.
Bangs it in short on off, Waller ducks under it.
Malcolm Waller is the new man in.

OUT! Peter what have you done? He has thrown it away. That was needless from him. The bowling change has done the trick. Asela flights it full on middle, Moor tries to loft it over long on but holes out. Kumara runs a little to his left, settles under the ball and takes a good catch. The umpire check whether the front foot is fine or no. It is marginal but he has something behind the line. A poor shot has resulted in another wicket.
Peter Moor has been caught at long on. The umpires are checking for the no ball.
Flatter on middle, Moor defends it by covering the line of the ball.
Full ball on off, Craig drives it uppishly through covers for a run.
Bowls it on off, turning away slightly. Ervine defends it off the front foot.
Full ball on leg stump, Moor gets it off the inner half to fine leg for a run.
Floats it on off, Moor defends it off the front foot.
Asela Gunaratne comes into the attack.
Lands it on a length on off, the batsman defends it off the front foot.
Full on off, Ervine drives it to mid off.
Bangs it in short, Moor pulls it over square leg for a run.
Good length outside off, Ervine punches it through cover-point for a run.
A tad shorter again outside off, the batsman pushes it through covers for a couple. Lakmal has been bowling a bit too short today.
EDGY FOUR! Bowls it on a length outside off, Ervine gets an outside edge and the ball races to the third man fence.
Suranga Lakmal is back into the attack.
Flighted ball on off, Ervine drives it through mid on for a run.
Drags his length back a little on middle, Peter punches it down to mid on for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Angles it in with the arm, Moor tries to defend it but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Tosses it up on leg stump, Craig sweeps it through backward square leg for a run.
Quicker through the air on middle, Ervine tries working it on the leg side but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Driven to mid on by the batsman. One run added to the total.

FOUR! EASY PICKINGS! Short and wide outside off, Ervine cuts it through point. Asela in the deep makes good ground to his right, dives but is unable to push the ball back in. Boundary to the batsman. Craig is playing a good innings here.
Very full on off, Peter slog sweeps it through mid-wicket for a run.
Tosses it outside off, the batsman drives it through covers for a couple.
Bowls it flatter on leg stump, Peter defends it off the back foot.
Full ball, Moor drives it back to the bowler.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Loopy ball on off, the batsman defends it off the front foot.
Gives it air on off, Moor drives it down to long on for a run.
Bowled on the pads, Moor sweeps it through backward square leg for a couple.
Drifts it down the leg side, Peter misses the flick.
Sprays on the pads, Moor misses his flick and it goes through to the keeper who fumbles. No run taken.
Drags his length back a little outside off, the batsman cuts it to point.
Full ball outside off, Ervine drives it to covers.
Loopy ball outside off, Ervine defends it off the front foot.
Sweeps it with the spin through mid-wicket for a run.
Quicker on off, Moor defends it off the back foot.
Flicks it with the angle through mid-wicket for a run.
SIX! BANG! Tosses it up on off, Moor goes down on one knee and slogs it over wide long on for a maximum. A great shot there, should get him going.
Full on off, Moor drives it to short extra cover who half stops it. But no run conceded.
Short leg moves to silly point now.
Flighted on off, Peter defends it off the front foot.
Full ball on leg, Ervine drives it down to long on for a run.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
EDGED BUT SHORT! Bowls it around off and gets it to skid away. Ervine tries to defend it but gets an outside edge on the bounce to first slip. He played that with soft hands.
Flatter on middle, the batsman defends it by covering the line of the ball.
Flighted on off, Moor defends it off the front foot.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.

IT'S A NO BALL! That's the end of the story there itself! Tosses it beautifully outside off, Moor tries to drive it but is beaten. Dickwella takes the bails off and appeals. The umpire goes upstairs to check. They first check the front foot of the bowler and guess what, he has overstepped. They need not look further.
There is a stumping appeal against Peter Moor. Seems safe though.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tries to play with spin but is struck on the pads.
That was close to the off stump. Tosses the ball up outside off, gets a little turn into the batsman who goes for the sweep but misses.
Flighted ball on off, Moor drives it to long off for a run.
Sprays it down the leg side, Moor misses the flick and the keeper collects it down the leg side.
Loopy ball outside off, Craig guides it towards point for a run.
Floats it on off, Peter drives it to long off for a run.
Gives it a lot of air on leg, Moor drives it back to the bowler.
Full ball on the pads, Ervine flicks it through square leg for a run.
Quicker ball on leg stump, stays a touch low. Peter does well to get his bat down in time.
Flighted ball, turning back in. Moor turns it to short leg.
Flatter and short outside off, Craig cuts it to sweeper cover for a run.
Loopy ball on off, Ervine defends it off the front foot.
Full outside off, Ervine lets it through to the keeper.
Tosses it up on off, Ervine drives it towards covers where the fielder makes a good diving stop.
Dilruwan Perera comes back into the attack.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floats it on off, goes on with the arm. Moor gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Drags his length back a little on off, Moor defends it off the back foot.
Quicker ball, full and outside off, Moor shoulders his arms to it.
Loopy ball on off, Moor defends it watchfully.
Tosses it up on middle, Moor defends it off the front foot.

Drinks has been taken. Another good passage of play for the home side. Zimbabwe started the second session nicely and the duo of Ervine and Raza added runs at a steady rate. However, the wily Herath got the better of the latter to pick up his third wicket. Sri Lanka are on top and it will need something courageous on the part of the visitors to fightback.
Full delivery attacking the stumps, turned to mid-wicket.
Yorker on off, Ervine does well to jam it out to mid on.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Length delivery on off, Ervine keeps it out.
Back of a length on middle, tucked to the leg side for a single.
Full length delivery outside off, eased through covers for a single.
Well bowled! Comes in with the arm, Moor is hurried on by it and gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Peter Moor strides out to the middle.

OUT! There is no inside edge, Zimbabwe waste a review! Tossed up around off, coming in with the arm. Raza prods forward and looks to keep it out with his bat and pad together. The Lankans appeal confidently in unison and umpire Nigel Llong decides to rule it out. However, Sikandar opts for the review straightaway. The replays roll in and from the close view angle, it shows that it is pad first and then the bat. Time for the Hawk Eye. It shows that the ball is going to crash into the middle and off stump. A good knock from him comes to an end. Important breakthrough for Sri Lanka. They have broken the 84-run stand.
Sikandar Raza has been given out LBW and he has taken a review straightaway. There might be an inside edge.
Kneels and paddles it down to fine leg for a single.
The batsman drives this through the covers. They pick up a single.

Well bowled! He keeps on making subtle changes of pace which keep the batsmen guessing. Raza uses his feet and looks to play it with the angle but is hit on the pads. The ball rolls past the slip fielder.
Floated around off, Raza defends it with his bat and pad close together. The short leg fielder is the only one appealing but there was no pad involved.
High full toss on leg stump, Raza clips it through square leg for a run. Surely that was not intentional, must have slipped out from the hand.
Good length delivery on off, Sikandar rises on his toes to block it.
Short of a length delivery, Ervine is a bit opened up in his stance but manages to play it with an angled bat to point. A run taken.

FOUR! Well played! Shortish delivery outside off, Ervine punches it beautifully through covers. He has timed that brilliantly and gets the desired result! Shows that this is a good track to bat on if you get your eye in.
Fullish delivery on the boots, Sikandar clips it through mid-wicket for a single.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Ervine punches it off the back foot to deep point for a run. These two have been really good. Have kept the scoreboard ticking.
Floated around the pads, Ervine nudges it to fine leg for a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Loopy delivery in line of the stumps, defended solidly off the front foot.
Tossed up on middle and leg, turned to short mid-wicket.
Floated outside off, Raza knocks it down to long off for a single.
Coming in with the arm, Raza hangs back and defends it tentatively.
Rangana Herath is back on.
Angling into the southpaw, tucked to short mid-wicket.

That's a good bouncer from Kumara. He steams in and hits the deck hard. It's climbing on Craig who has to take evasive action. The fast bowler gives the batsman a stare. Aggression from him, good to see.
Back of a length and width on offer, Ervine goes for the cut but gets beaten.
Length delivery angling in from outside off, Ervine stays back and blocks it.
Kumara comes from around the wicket and bowls a fullish delivery in line of the stumps, pushed back to the bowler off the inner half.
Good length delivery outside off, Raza punches it to sweeper cover for a single.
A bit short on middle and leg, turned around the corner for a run.
4th Test fifty for Craig Ervine.

Tossed up in line of the stumps, eased through mid on for a run. It has been a composed knock from the southpaw to reach his half century. He has looked solid in the middle and punished the loose deliveries. His side needs him to convert this one into a big one.
Loopy delivery around off, played with soft hands to covers.
SIX! What a confident shot! A bit short on off, Ervine is quick to transfer his weight on the back foot and pulls it over wide long on for half a dozen. He is taking on Perera. Moves to 49 with that.
Floated around off, Craig lunges forward in defense.
FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished! Short and width on offer, Ervine rocks back and cuts it through point to find the fence.
Good length delivery slanting across Craig. He steers it behind point for a single.
On a length on off, Ervine plants his front foot forward and defends it back to the bowler.

Fullish delivery well outside off, Raza goes at it with hard hands but gets it off the toe end behind point. The ball rolls towards the fence but the fielder does well to keep the ball in play. Three runs taken.
Herath has a word with Chandimal. Might be about the field placements.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Raza uses the depth of the crease and punches it through covers. Good running between the wickets allows the batsmen to come back for two.
Length delivery on off, pushed to mid off for a quick single.

Close shave! Good length delivery on off, Raza taps it towards cover-point and sets off. His partner responds. However, Sikandar hesitates a bit and eventually goes through with the run. There is a shy at the striker's end but it misses. Had it hit, it would have been close.
Lahiru Kumara is back on.
Shorter this time outside off, Ervine punches it to covers.
Slow through the air outside off, pushed to covers.
Fullish on off, tapped to covers.
50-run stand up between Ervine and Raza.
Tossed up on middle, whipped through mid-wicket for a brace.
Tossed up on middle, defended to short leg where Mendis is sharp as a hawk. Dean Jones on air says that he is one of the best fielders in that region.
FOUR! Good use of the feet and he gets the desired result! Floated outside off, Ervine dances down the track, gets right to the pitch of it and lifts it over mid off for a boundary.
Sharp bouncer on off, Raza ducks under it to evade it.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full length delivery on middle, Ervine plays it towards mid on for a run.
Good length delivery outside off, Craig guides it through point. Two runs taken.
Shortish delivery outside off, Ervine cuts it to point.
Good length delivery angling into Ervine. He camps back and blocks it.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Raza stays back and nudges it behind square on the leg side for a couple.
Straying on the pads, tucked to square leg for a single.
Tossed up outside off, Raza uses his feet ans gets it off the inner half through mid-wicket. A run taken.
Raza uses his feet but Perera tosses this one up nicely on middle. He blocks it.
Quicker one outside off, tapped to covers for a single.
Short delivery outside off, Sikandar ducks under it.
FOUR! Good shot! Good length delivery outside off, Raza gets into position quickly and pulls it confidently through mid-wicket. Struck that well and the ball races to the fence.
Good length delivery in line of the stumps, worked to short mid-wicket.
Shortish delivery outside off, punched through point for a run.
On a length in line of the stumps, defended solidly off the back foot.
Outside off, Ervine lets it go.
Floated on middle, Raza lunges forward in defense.
On the shorter side, Sikandar tucks it to mid-wicket.
Loopy delivery outside off, turning in. Raza stays back to keep it out.
Hangs back to the shorter delivery and works it to wide mid on for a run.
Slow through the air on off, Ervine looks to clip it across but is a touch early into his stroke. Gets a soft leading edge that rolls back to the bowler.
Tossed up outside off, played with an open face towards point.
Dilruwan Perera to bowl from the other end.
Length ball on off, turned to mid-wicket.
Similar length delivery on middle and off, Raza covers the line and blocks it.
Full length delivery in line of the stumps, Craig pats it towards mid off to rotate strike.
FOUR! Crisp! Fullish delivery slanting across Ervine. He leans into it and strokes it elegantly through covers to find the fence.
That's a peach! Bowls it in the off stump channel and gets it to angle away. Ervine goes forward to push at it but gets beaten all ends up.
Starts off with a length ball around off, Ervine plants his front foot across and sees it through safely.
We are back for the afternoon session. Craig Ervine and Sikandar Raza will continue their innings. Suranga Lakmal will bowl first up after the break. He has two slips in place.
...Day 1, Session 2...

Zimbabwe on the other hand, would look to build partnerships. Craig Ervine is playing a steady innings and has got good support from Sikandar Raza who has come out with intent and has struck the ball well. The visitors would hope for these two to continue for as long as possible. The wicket is taking a little turn but nothing threatening. Still a good enough wicket to bat on if the batsmen apply themselves. Do join us in a short while.

So, Sri Lanka will be the happier of the two sides after the first session. Zimbabwe after electing to bat had a steady start. They played the new ball well. The introduction of the spinners changed things for them and the visitors lost four wickets in quick succession. The hosts would want to continue the same after the break and keep the pressure on the away side.
Good thinking by Kumara! He bowls a full length delivery on off, Raza hangs back and manages to keep it out. THAT'S LUNCH ON DAY 1!
A leg slip comes into place for the last ball before lunch.
Kumara switches back to over the wicket. He bowls a well-directed bouncer on off, Raza ducks under it to evade it.
Shortish delivery on leg stump, helped on its way to fine leg for a single.
Full length delivery attacking the stumps, Craig plays it with soft hands to mid on.
Kumara comes around the wicket and angles in a good length ball on off, Ervine pats it to the off side.
Short of a length delivery slanting across Ervine. He plays a confident back foot punch to short extra cover.
A touch short this time, Raza camps back and keeps it out.
Tosses this one nicely again and outside off, spins in a touch. Sikandar puts his head down and defends it calmly.
Slow through the air on off, Raza leans forward to block it.
Floated on middle, knocked down to wide long on for a single.
Floated in line of the stumps, Ervine lunges forward in defense.
A bit short on off, Raza rocks back and punches it to the left of mid off. A run taken.
Back of a length delivery slanting across Ervine. He hangs back and pushes it to short cover.
Straying on the hips this time, Raza hops and turns it to fine leg for a run.
A well-directed bouncer on off, Sikandar ducks under it.
Good bowling by Kumara! Bends his back and bowls a back of a length delivery on off, Raza hops back and defends it to short leg.
On a good length, angling away from the southpaw. He steers it to third man for a run.
Short of a length delivery angling across Ervine. He camps back and defends it.
Lahiru Kumara comes back into the attack.
Floated outside off, Raza takes a big stride forward and blocks it.
Floated outside off, defended off the front foot.

FOUR! Shot! He is looking to dominate the spinners and it is working at the moment. Crouches to a tossed up delivery around off and sweeps it hard through front of square leg. Tharanga in the deep has no chance to cut it off.
Tossed up around off, Ervine kneels and paddles it to fine leg for a run.
This one comes in with the arm. Ervine uses the depth of the crease and punches it back to the bowler.
Leans ahead to the flighted delivery and blocks it.
Full on middle, Craig turns it through mid-wicket for a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Fullish delivery on middle, Ervine drives it crisply to the left of Herath who dives to his left to make a good stop.
Raza brings out the paddle sweep into play and gets it to fine leg. A run taken.
Loopy ball on middle and leg, swept around the corner for a run.
Floated delivery, Ervine prods forward to defend it.
Flatter on off, Ervine rocks back and punches it to long off for a run.
Fullish on off, a confident front foot defense from Craig.
Coming in with the arm, Ervine looks to play it across but is pinged on the pads. A stifled appeal for an LBW is turned down. It was clearly heading down leg.
Loopy ball on off, Ervine lunges forward in defense.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.
A bit short on middle, turned through wide mid on for a run.
Goes back to the flatter delivery and eases it to covers.
Fullish on middle, patted back to the bowler.
Driven through the mid on region. One run added to the total.
Tossed up on middle, Sikandar skips down the track and wrists it past the left side of the diving short mid-wicket fielder. A single taken. A bit risky but safe in the end.
Full on middle and leg, Raza kneels and paddles it to fine leg for a couple.

SIX! This is a stroke of a man high on confidence! Floated on middle, Raza uses his feet and lifts it over the bowler's head for a maximum. That was clean as a whistle. This was similar to the shot with which he won the ODI series for his side.
Pushed quicker through the air, turns away sharply. Ervine looks to play at it first but bails out. End of a successful over for Sri Lanka.
Sikandar Raza comes out to bat.

OUT! Williams throws his wicket away! He plays the conventional sweeps and reverse sweeps well but attempting the slog sweep has brought about his downfall. Floated outside off on a fullish length, Sean kneels and goes for the slog sweep but fails to get on the top of the bounce. As a result, it takes the top edge of his bat and skies in the air behind square on the leg side. Asela Gunaratne goes across to his left, lines it up and takes a comfortable catch. Sri Lanka are on top and the spinners are getting the breakthroughs on a consistent basis.
Fullish outside off, pushed back to the bowler.
Once again it's on the leg stump line, whipped to square leg.
Straying on the pads, Sean turns it past short leg. Two runs taken.
Stays back to the loopy delivery on off and blocks it.
Fullish outside off, Craig gets on the front foot to defend it.
In the air... but safe! Tossed up around off, turning in. Ervine is early into his drive and as a result, it goes uppishly towards Herath. Thankfully for him it carries to Rangana on the bounce.
Slow through the air, Ervine pats it to covers.
FOUR! Nice improvisation! Fullish delivery on off, Ervine kneels and reverse sweeps it through point to pick up a boundary. He plays that shot really well.
Loopy ball on off, once again Ervine leans forward confidently to block it.
Floated around off, Ervine lunges forward and keeps it out.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Quicker and flatter again on leg stump, Ervine tucks it through square leg. Lakmal in the deep covers good ground to his right and saves a run for his side.
Flatter delivery on leg, Williams nudges it around the corner for a run.
Floated outside off, swept to fine leg for a single.
Fullish on off, defended solidly off the front foot.
Floated around off, Craig lunges forward in defense.
Dilruwan Perera comes on for a bowl.
A bit short outside off, Williams guides it towards third man. Good running between the wickets allows them to come back for two.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Beautiful! Tossed up outside off, Williams leans ahead and strokes it elegantly through wide mid off. Has timed it well and the ball whistles away to the fence.
Flatter delivery, Williams keeps it out.
Loopy around off, Sean presses forward and defends it.
Tossed up outside off, Ervine uses his feet and blocks it off the inner half past the bowler.
FOUR! Well controlled! Back of a length delivery around off, Williams arches back and guides it over gully to find the fence.
Driven through the covers by the batsman.
On a length on middle, tapped to mid off for a quick single.

Aggression from Kumara! Full delivery in line of the stumps, Craig drives it back to Kumara who does well to stop it in his followthrough. Throws it back on the stumps at the striker's end and the keeper does well to collect it. Lahiru is interested for the run out but the batsman is safe.
Full length delivery in line of the stumps, Ervine defends it calmly. Ian Gould is having a word with Kumara as he is getting close to the danger zone.
Good length delivery angling across Ervine. Played with an open face to point.
Floated outside off, Williams stays back and defends it.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Stays back to this one and blocks it to the off side.
Loopy ball around off, defended solidly off the front foot.
FOUR! Fullish delivery on off, Williams brings out the fancy reverse sweep. Only manages to get some bat on it and gets it between the keeper and the slip fielder. Another boundary results.
Herath is bowling with great control! Tosses this one nicely outside off, Williams prods forward to defend but gets beaten all ends up.
Another short delivery, Ervine sways away from the line of it to evade it.
Dug in short, Craig sits under the bumper.
Fuller length outside off, played towards wide mid off for a run.
FOUR! Confident stroke! Back of a length ball slanting across Williams. He hangs back and punches it with authority wide of point to pick up a boundary.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Well bowled! Length delivery slanting across Williams. He pokes at it but gets beaten all ends up.
Floated outside off, Ervine lunges forward in defense.

Close shave! Quicker one in line of the stumps, Ervine turns it to the left of Mendis at short leg. He crouches and makes a sharp stop but misses his shy at the striker's end. Ervine who was out of his crease for a moment dives to get in. Good effort.
Floated around off, Ervine  plays it with an open face to the off side.
Slower through the air outside off, Ervine defends it to short leg.
Fullish delivery outside off, defended off the front foot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fuller length ball, slanting across Williams. He doesn't fiddle with it. Wicket maiden for Kumara.
Dug in short, Williams ducks under it.
Sean Williams comes out to bat.

OUT! Successful review for the home side! Kumara steams in and bowls a fuller length ball outside off. It is angling in and then straightens. Musakanda goes for a booming drive but seems to have missed it as the ball sails into the gloves of Dickwella. However, there is a bit of noise which gets the Sri Lankans interested.  Dinesh Chandimal has a chat with the keeper and the bowler and decides to go for the review. The replays show that the ball was very close to the outside edge as it went through. There is no Hot Spot or Snicko available and the third umpire overturns the onfield decision on the basis of sound which was heard. The debutant, Musakanda is not happy with it but he has to walk back. Zimbabwe are in a state of bother now.
Was there edge? Sri Lanka have taken a review for caught behind against Musakanda.
Kumara opts to bang the deck hard and bowls it short. Tarisai ducks under it.
Full length ball outside off, driven crisply to wide mid off.
Back of a length delivery, angling in from outside off. Musakanda hangs back and pats it to covers.
Lahiru Kumara is introduced into the attack. Two slips in place.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Craig Ervine is the new man in.

Time for Drinks. A great first hour of play for Sri Lanka. Zimbabwe started off cautiously and were going quite well. The introduction of Rangana Herath changed things. His two wickets have put Zimbabwe on the back foot and they are looking tentative against the wily old fox and need to pick him.

OUT! Mendis you beauty! Loopy ball on middle, skids through. Hamilton tries to defend it but gets an inside edge and Kusal at short leg dives forward to take an excellent catch. Zimbabwe have lost both their openers and not the start they wanted after electing to bat first.
It's been driven superbly through the covers.

An appeal again, Herath is making a lot of things happen. Tosses it up on middle, does not turn. Masakadza tries to play it off the front foot but is pinged on the pads. The Lankans go up but the umpire shakes his head. Missing leg clearly.
HUGE APPEAL! Bowls an arm ball on middle, Masakadza tries to sweep but misses and is hit on the pads. They appeal but the umpire gives it not out. Going down with the angle.
Floats it on off, Hamilton defends it off the front foot.
FOUR! Bangs it in short outside off, Musakanda tries to pull it but gets a top edge through fine leg for a boundary. First boundary in his Test career.
Lands it on a length on off, Hamilton plays it with soft hands to cover and takes a run.
BOUNCER! That took off. Batsman does well to duck under it. The keeper jumps and takes it with one hand.
Back of a length on off, Hamilton defends it watchfully.
A tad fuller outside off, Musakanda drives it towards extra cover for a run.
Good length on off, defended off the back foot.
Dances down the track and mistimes his drive to mid off.
First run for Musakanda in Test cricket! Tosses it on middle, he gets it off the inner half through backward square leg for a run.
Plays the paddle sweep through short fine leg. Lakmal makes good ground to his right in the deep and dives to stop a boundary. The batsmen take three.
Loopy ball on leg stump, goes on with the arm. Masakadza tries to defend it but misses and gets hit on the pads. There is a stifled appeal but nothing from the umpire. That was missing leg clearly.
Flighted this time on off, Hamilton defends it by covering the line of the ball.
Flatter and angling into the batsman. Masakadza flicks it through wide mid on for a couple.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
A tad shorter outside off, Masakadza mistimes his cut to covers for a run.
Straighter this time, Hamilton flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple.
Driven towards the mid on region.
Good length on off, the batsman defends it solidly.
Back of a length on off, Masakadza defends it off the back foot.
Floated it on off, Musakanda defends it watchfully. A great first over from Herath.
Tosses it up on middle, Musakanda defends it off the front foot.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
The debutant, Tarisai Musakanda strides out to bat.

OUT! Herath strikes! Lovely bowling! The ball before this turned away and this one went on with the arm. Loopy ball on off, Chakabva plays all around it and it goes through bat and pad to shatter the stumps. First one down for Zimbabwe and who else but Rangana Herath provides the breakthrough for the home side.
BEATEN! Beautifully bowled! Tosses it up on off, the batsman tries to defend it off the front foot but gets beaten by the away turn.
Bowls it on the pads, Chakabva flicks it down to fine leg for a couple.
Rangana Herath comes into the attack. A slip and short leg in place. He is the go-to man for Sri Lanka. A lot will be expected from him.
Back of a length on middle, Chakabva nudges it towards square leg for a run.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.
Good length on middle, the batsman works it through square leg for a couple.
Drifts it on the pads, Chakabva flicks it through backward square leg for a couple.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Driven to mid on by the batsman.
Lands it on a length on off, Masakadza plays it to mid off.
FOUR! Short ball on middle, Masakadza pulls it through backward square leg for a boundary.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Good length and angling into the batsman, Hamilton flicks it to mid on.
Back of a length outside off, Masakadza punches it to point.
Bowls it full on middle, Chakabva flicks it off the inner half through square leg for a couple.
Good length outside off, the batsman shoulders his arms to it.
Lands it on a length on off, Chakabva defends it with soft hands.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it. Lakmal has been moving close to the danger area. The umpire is having a close look at him.
Length ball outside off, Chakabva lets it through to the keeper.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

NOT OUT! Sri Lanka lose a review early in the game. Kumara lands it on a length outside off, jags back in a touch. Masakadza tries to defend it with his bat and pad close together. The Lankans appeal but the umpire turns it down. They feel it has hit the pad first and Chandimal after a chat with his teammates decides to review. Replays show that the front foot is fine. The ball strikes him on the pad first and then on the bat but the impact is marginally outside off. Also, it is only clipping the top of middle stump. The on-field call stays. It looked really close, not a bad review by Sri Lanka.
Dinesh Chandimal has opted to take a review against Hamilton Masakadza. Is is pad first?

BIG APPEAL! Lands it on a length on middle, swings in a little. Masakadza tries to defend it but misses and is struck on the pads. There is a big appeal but the umpire gives it not out. Might be missing leg.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Lands it on a length outside off, Hamilton shoulders his arms to it.
Shorter in length on off, Masakadza defends it off the back foot.
EDGED BUT SHORT! A tad fuller on off shaping away from the batsman, Chakabva pokes at it and gets an edge which falls short of second slip. A maiden for Lakmal.
Bowls it on a length, Chakabva defends it solidly.
Back of a length on off, Regis defends it off the back foot.
Good length outside off, the batsman does not bother playing a shot at it.
Length ball outside off, Chakabva lets it through to the keeper.
Lands it on a length on middle, Chakabva defends it off the front foot.
Fuller length ball outside off, Masakadza gets a bottom edge onto his pads.
FOUR! Short ball outside off, Hamilton cuts it past the diving point fielder for a boundary. First boundary of the day.
Good length on middle, Hamilton defends it off the front foot.
A tad fuller on middle, the batsman flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
WIDE! You don't see a wide bowled often in Test cricket. Bowls it very wide outside off, Chakabva lets it through.
Sprays it down the leg side, Chakabva lets it through to the keeper.
Bangs it in short outside off, Hamilton cuts it to point who dives to his left and makes a partial stop. A run taken.
Lahiru Kumara to bowl from the other end. Two slips in place for him as well.
Fullish ball on off, Masakadza drives it towards wide mid off. The fielder runs to his left and dives to make a half stop. They run a single. Zimbabwe are underway.
Good length just outside off, Masakadza points his bat skywards and lets it go.
Lands it on a fuller length on middle, the batsman defends it off the front foot.
Gets some shape away from the batsman outside off, Hamilton lets it through to the keeper.
A tad fuller outside off, Masakadza shoulders his arms to it.
Starts off with a full outswinger on off, Hamilton drives it to point. A good confident drive there by the batsman.

The players are out for their respective National Anthems. After the completion, we are ready to get going. Tarisai Musakanda has been handed over his Test cap by the skipper. A big moment for him. Hamilton Masakadza and Regis Chakabva to open the batting for Zimbabwe. Suranga Lakmal to start the proceedings with the ball. Two slips in place. Here we go...

Sri Lanka skipper, Dinesh Chandimal says that they would have batted first as well but the toss is not in their control. He is thankful to the Sri Lankan Cricket Board for choosing him as the captain. Adds that he will give his heart and soul to the job. Credits Zimbabwe for playing outstanding cricket in the ODIs. Adds that they have plans and strategies against them for this game. States that it is a good track. Ends by saying that they are looking to restrict the opposition under 300.

Zimbabwe skipper, Graeme Cremer says, he will bat first. He feels it's a good wicket for batting. Reckons that the wicket has been rolled out well. Mentions they have to be good with the bat and the wicket might take turn after the second day. Admits the mood in the dressing room is great and there are no injuries.

Pitch Report - Alistair Campbell and Russel Arnold doing the pitch report say that batting first is the way to go. Add that it is nice and hard with even covering of grass. State that there will be good carry. Mention that the red ball will swing for the first hour or so. End by saying that the track will slow down as the game progresses.
Toss - Zimbabwe win the toss and opt to bat.

Zimbabwe on the other hand, will be high on confidence. It is a different format altogether and they will have to bring their A game to the fore. The home side are favorites on paper, but as we saw in the ODIs, cricket is a funny game and you can't rule the Zimbabweans out. The forecast for the coming five days is not that good and let's hope the rain does not play spoilsport. Stay tuned for the toss.

Hello and welcome to the first and only Test between Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe in Colombo. After Angelo Mathews stepped down as captain from all formats, Dinesh Chandimal has been appointed as their 15th Test skipper. The hosts will have to pull themselves up after a shock series defeat in the ODIs. Nothing less then a win will be acceptable for Chandimal, against a team which is ranked 10th and has never defeated the Lankans in the longest format of the game. They would hope all their players stand up and deliver the goods.
